title: Home · Start here
text: labbayk aa en السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ your umrah, one step at a time. free. no sign-up. works offline. start umrah continue where you left off step 1 · before umrah install the guide use it offline, like an app. install where are you now? tap one. we take you straight to what you need to do. 1 at home, preparing 2 near the meeqat 3 arriving in makkah 4 at the masjid gate 5 doing tawaf 7 doing sa‘i umrah at a glance umrah has 4 essential acts , always in this order: ihram enter the state tawaf 7 rounds sa‘i 7 laps hair shave or cut most pilgrims finish in a few hours, depending on crowds. you may rest between acts. see the full journey map start here what is umrah? who can perform umrah? what should i prepare? essential checklist what is umrah? a short pilgrimage to makkah that can be done at almost any time of year. it is sometimes called the “lesser pilgrimage”, to tell it apart from hajj. who can perform it? any muslim: men, women, children, elderly and disabled pilgrims. a wheelchair or help from others is fine. is it obligatory? scholars differ. some say once in a lifetime for those able; others say it is a strongly recommended sunnah. help & guidance duas & dhikr women’s guidance elderly, disabled & families questions & mistakes quick reference lost? my info card content reviewed by [reviewing scholar / institution]. sources & notes

title: Umrah journey map
text: overview umrah journey b · journey map 8 steps. start with step 1. tap any step to open it. steps with the essential label are the 4 acts every umrah must include. 01 before umrah papers, packing, learning the steps. 02 ihram enter the sacred state at the meeqat. say the talbiyah. essential 03 entering makkah check in, rest, make wudu. 04 entering masjid al-haram right foot first. go to the tawaf area. 05 tawaf 7 rounds around the ka‘bah, ka‘bah on your left. essential 06 after tawaf pray 2 rak‘ahs. drink zamzam. 07 sa‘i 7 laps between safa and marwah. start at safa. essential 08 halq / taqsir shave or shorten the hair. this ends ihram. essential umrah complete ihram restrictions are lifted. alhamdulillah. a note on “essential” schools classify these acts differently (pillar or obligation), but every pilgrim performs all four. read the notes home start · step 1 before umrah

title: Step 1 · Before Umrah
text: step 1 of 8 before umrah 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 01 before umrah get your papers, your body and your heart ready. where am i? at home, before you travel what do i do now? tick as you go. your ticks are saved on this phone. papers visa. umrah is allowed on an umrah visa or a saudi visit/tourist visa. umrah permit in the nusuk app. book your umrah time slot in the official nusuk app. you can’t enter for umrah before your permit time. passport valid for at least 6 months from your travel date. confirm with your airline or agent. meningitis vaccine (all pilgrims). acyw or acywx conjugate vaccine within the last 5 years (or polysaccharide within 3 years), at least 10 days before arrival. only if it applies to you: polio or yellow fever vaccines for arrivals from listed countries (pakistan and afghanistan are on the polio list). covid-19 proof for people over 65, pregnant women and those with chronic illness. hotel address and group leader’s number, saved on your phone and on paper. checked september 2026 · health: saudi ministry of health, umrah health requirements 1447h (2026) · permits and visas: ministry of hajj and umrah faq · passport: travel industry guidance. rules can change each season; check again before booking. bookings (nusuk and travel) create your nusuk account (official app of the ministry of hajj and umrah). all permits and umrah bookings run through it. umrah visa: hotel booked through nusuk masar. since the 1447h season, a confirmed booking in a licensed hotel, recorded in nusuk masar, is required before an umrah visa is issued. your agent or nusuk does this. umrah permit for your chosen date and time, in the nusuk app (see papers above). train (optional): the haramain high speed railway links jeddah airport (king abdulaziz international), jeddah, makkah and madinah. makkah to madinah takes about 2 hours. book only through the official saudi arabia railways (sar) channels. visiting madinah? book a rawdah (riyad al-jannah) permit in the nusuk app. it is free; men and women have separate times and gates; you can only enter in your booked slot. checked september 2026 · nusuk masar hotel rule: ministry of hajj and umrah (reported by saudi gazette, june 2025) · train: saudi arabia railways / visit saudi · rawdah: nusuk app rules as reported september 2026. booking rules change often; check in the nusuk app before you travel. pack men: 2 plain white ihram sheets, a belt, open sandals. women: loose, modest clothes that cover the body. any colour. unscented soap, shampoo and deodorant (for use in ihram). your medicines in original packs, with prescriptions. small bag, water bottle, power bank, a bag for your shoes. heart & mind learn the 4 essential acts: ihram, tawaf, sa‘i, hair. practise the talbiyah (see step 2). renew your intention, repent, settle debts, ask forgiveness from people you may have wronged. what do i say? when your journey starts سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ، وَإِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ subḥāna-lladhī sakhkhara lanā hādhā wa mā kunnā lahū muqrinīn, wa innā ilā rabbinā la-munqalibūn. meaning: glory be to the one who has placed this at our service; we could not have done it ourselves. and to our lord we will surely return. qur’an 43:13–14 · part of the travel dua in sahih muslim 1342 remember men: practise wearing ihram at home try tying the sheets and belt once before you travel. expect a lot of walking sa‘i alone is about 3 km. break in comfortable sandals before you go. avoid leaving all the learning until you arrive. you will be tired. packing only scented toiletries. you can’t use them in ihram. map next · step 2 enter ihram

title: Step 2 · Ihram
text: step 2 of 8 ihram 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 02 · essential ihram الإحرام the sacred state of umrah. you enter it with an intention and the talbiyah . the clothes alone are not ihram. where am i? before you pass the meeqat the meeqat is a boundary you must not cross without ihram. on a plane, the crew usually announces it. your group leader will tell you which one you pass. the five meeqat dhul-hulayfah (abyar ‘ali) coming from madinah al-juhfah (rabigh) coming from the north-west: syria, egypt, north africa qarn al-manazil (as-sayl al-kabir) coming from najd and the east yalamlam (as-sa‘diyyah) coming from yemen and the south dhat ‘irq coming from iraq already in makkah? go outside the haram boundary, e.g. masjid ‘a’ishah at tan‘im, and enter ihram there. sahih al-bukhari 1524, sahih muslim 1181; dhat ‘irq: sahih al-bukhari 1531 what do i do now? 1 get clean. trim nails, remove unwanted hair, take a full bath (ghusl). men may put perfume on the body, not the clothes, before the intention. sunnah 2 put on ihram clothes. see “men” and “women” below. must 3 pray, if it is a prayer time. it is good to enter ihram after a prayer. scholars differ many scholars recommend 2 rak‘ahs for ihram; others say there is no special ihram prayer. 4 at or before the meeqat, make the intention. intend umrah in your heart and say: “labbayka ‘umratan.” must 5 say the talbiyah often. men aloud, women quietly. keep saying it until you begin tawaf. sunnah men two white, unstitched sheets: one round the waist, one over the shoulders. head uncovered. open sandals. women your normal loose, modest clothes, any colour. no niqab and no gloves. more for women what do i say? 1 · intention at the meeqat لَبَّيْكَ عُمْرَةً labbayka ‘umratan meaning: here i am, o allah, for umrah. based on the prophet’s ﷺ wording “labbayka ‘umratan wa ḥajjan” for umrah with hajj · sahih muslim 1251 2 · talbiyah, again and again لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ labbayka-llāhumma labbayk. labbayka lā sharīka laka labbayk. inna-l-ḥamda wa-n-ni‘mata laka wa-l-mulk. lā sharīka lak. meaning: here i am, o allah, here i am. here i am, you have no partner, here i am. all praise and blessings are yours, and all dominion. you have no partner. sahih al-bukhari 1549 · sahih muslim 1184 optional · if you fear you may not finish (illness, age) اللَّهُمَّ مَحِلِّي حَيْثُ حَبَسْتَنِي allāhumma maḥillī ḥaythu ḥabastanī meaning: o allah, i will leave ihram wherever you stop me. sahih al-bukhari 5089 · sahih muslim 1207 now in ihram: avoid perfume or scented soap, cream or wipes cutting or removing hair or nails marital relations and intimacy; a marriage contract hunting animals arguing, bad language, sins men: fitted, stitched clothing (shirts, trousers, underwear); covering the head women: niqab and gloves qur’an 2:197 · sahih al-bukhari 1542, 1838 allowed in ihram showering with unscented soap · changing your ihram sheets · watch, glasses, belt, money pouch · umbrella · bandages and medicine. remember flying in? most scholars say enter ihram before the plane passes the meeqat, not after landing at jeddah. some allow jeddah for certain routes. follow your scholar. made a mistake in ihram? don’t panic. things done by forgetting or not knowing are treated gently; some mistakes need a compensation (fidyah). ask a scholar. back next · step 3 enter makkah

title: Step 3 · Entering Makkah
text: step 3 of 8 entering makkah 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 03 entering makkah مكة you are in ihram now. keep saying the talbiyah, settle in, and get ready for the masjid. where am i? on the way to makkah / at your hotel what do i do now? 1 keep saying the talbiyah on the way. sunnah 2 check in and rest if you need to. it is fine to sleep or eat before tawaf. a rested pilgrim makes fewer mistakes. optional 3 take a bath if easy, then make wudu. the prophet ﷺ bathed before entering makkah. wudu is needed for tawaf. wudu: must for tawaf 4 agree a meeting point with your group. pick a masjid gate by its number and name. write it in my info . practical 5 take only what you need. water, phone, charger, a bag for your shoes, this guide. what do i say? the talbiyah labbayka-llāhumma labbayk… tap to see it in full. you can also remember allah in your own words, in any language. remember patience is part of your umrah expect crowds, heat and long walks. be gentle with others and with yourself. avoid leaving the hotel without knowing how to get back. take a photo of the hotel name and street. bath before entering makkah: sahih al-bukhari 1573 back next · step 4 enter the masjid

title: Step 4 · Entering Masjid al-Haram
text: step 4 of 8 entering the masjid 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 04 entering masjid al-haram the great mosque around the ka‘bah. enter calmly and walk to the tawaf area (the mataf ). where am i? at a gate of masjid al-haram what do i do now? 1 note your gate. take a photo of the gate number and name. put your shoes in your bag. practical 2 step in with your right foot and say the entry dua. sunnah 3 walk to the mataf. very crowded? tawaf on the upper floors is valid too. it is longer, but calmer. your choice 4 when you see the ka‘bah, make dua. ask allah for anything, in your own language. there is no fixed dua you must say here. 5 if the prayer is starting, join it first. then begin tawaf. what do i say? entering (right foot first) بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ، اللَّهُمَّ افْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ bismillāh, wa-ṣ-ṣalātu wa-s-salāmu ‘alā rasūlillāh. allāhumma-ftaḥ lī abwāba raḥmatik. meaning: in the name of allah, and peace and blessings on the messenger of allah. o allah, open for me the doors of your mercy. sahih muslim 713 · sunan abi dawud 465 remember if you get lost go to the nearest gate, read its number, and call your group. masjid staff can help. open my info avoid stopping in walkways for photos. letting children walk ahead without a meeting plan. women on their period wait before entering for tawaf. read what to do back next · step 5 begin tawaf

title: Step 5 · Tawaf
text: step 5 of 8 tawaf 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 05 · essential tawaf الطواف walk around the ka‘bah 7 times , with the ka‘bah on your left , starting and ending at the black stone. where am i? in the mataf, around the ka‘bah anticlockwise. ka‘bah always on your left . look for the green light on the masjid wall in line with the black stone. what do i do now? before you start have wudu. stop saying the talbiyah. men: uncover the right shoulder (sheet under the right arm, over the left shoulder), only for this tawaf. 1 stand in line with the black stone. intend tawaf in your heart. must 2 touch or kiss the black stone only if easy. usually it isn’t. just face it, raise your right hand toward it and say “allāhu akbar”. sunnah 3 walk with the ka‘bah on your left. go around the outside of the low curved wall (hijr isma‘il). it is part of the ka‘bah. must 4 men: walk briskly in rounds 1 to 3, if you can. short, quick steps (ramal). normal pace in rounds 4 to 7. skip it in heavy crowds. sunnah 5 at the yemeni corner, touch it with your right hand if easy. if not, just walk on. no need to point. sunnah 6 each time you pass the black stone line: one round done. raise your right hand and say “allāhu akbar”. tap the counter below. 7 after round 7, tawaf is complete. men: cover your right shoulder again. round counter you are on round 1 of 7 alhamdulillah 7 rounds done 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 i passed the black stone +1 undo lost count? go with the lower number you are sure of. what do i say? at the black stone, every round اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ allāhu akbar meaning: allah is the greatest. sahih al-bukhari 1613. many also say “bismillāh” first, reported from ibn ‘umar. between the yemeni corner and the black stone رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ rabbanā ātinā fi-d-dunyā ḥasanah, wa fi-l-ākhirati ḥasanah, wa qinā ‘adhāba-n-nār. meaning: our lord, give us good in this world and good in the hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the fire. qur’an 2:201 · sunan abi dawud 1892 the rest of the time: your own words there is no fixed dua for each round. make dua in any language, remember allah, or recite qur’an. more dhikr remember prayer called during tawaf? join the prayer where you are. then continue from that point. wudu broke during tawaf? leave, renew your wudu and come back. scholars differ on whether you continue or restart. ask your scholar. tired or in a wheelchair? tawaf in a wheelchair, or on the upper floors, is valid. see care guidance avoid these mistakes walking inside hijr isma‘il. that round does not count. pushing to reach the black stone. hurting others is a sin; touching it is only sunnah. touching the ka‘bah cloth in ihram. it is perfumed. loud group duas and stopping in the flow for photos. back next · step 6 after tawaf

title: Step 6 · After Tawaf
text: step 6 of 8 after tawaf 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 06 after tawaf pray two short rak‘ahs, drink zamzam, then head to safa for sa‘i. where am i? near maqam ibrahim, or anywhere in the masjid what do i do now? 1 men: cover both shoulders. 2 pray 2 rak‘ahs behind maqam ibrahim if there is space. if crowded, pray anywhere in the masjid. don’t pray in the path of people doing tawaf. recite surah al-kafirun and surah al-ikhlas, one in each rak‘ah (sahih muslim 1218). strongly recommended some scholars consider these 2 rak‘ahs required. 3 drink zamzam water and make dua. coolers of zamzam are all around the masjid. sunnah 4 if easy, touch the black stone once more. only if it is not crowded. otherwise skip it. sunnah, if easy 5 follow the signs to the mas‘a (safa and marwah). resting briefly first is fine. what do i say? walking to maqam ibrahim (optional) وَاتَّخِذُوا مِنْ مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ مُصَلًّى wattakhidhū min maqāmi ibrāhīma muṣallā. meaning: and take the standing place of ibrahim as a place of prayer. qur’an 2:125 · recited by the prophet ﷺ here, sahih muslim 1218 drinking zamzam ask allah for whatever you need, in your own words. “zamzam water is for whatever it is drunk for.” sunan ibn majah 3062 remember praying at sunrise, noon or sunset? some scholars say wait until these times pass; others allow these 2 rak‘ahs at any time. follow your scholar. multazam (optional) some companions made dua at the wall between the black stone and the door. only if not crowded, and don’t touch the perfumed cloth in ihram. back next · step 7 begin sa‘i at safa

title: Step 7 · Sa‘i
text: step 7 of 8 sa‘i 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 07 · essential sa‘i السعي walk between the hills of safa and marwah 7 times. start at safa, finish at marwah. about 3 km in all. where am i? the mas‘a: the long hall of safa and marwah what do i do now? 1 go to safa. as you get near, recite the verse (first time only). sunnah 2 on safa, face the ka‘bah and raise your hands. say “allāhu akbar” three times and the dhikr below, then make your own dua. repeat three times. sunnah 3 walk to marwah. that is lap 1. must: 7 laps, safa first 4 men: jog lightly between the green lights. women walk normally the whole way. sunnah 5 on marwah, face the ka‘bah and do the same as on safa. (not the verse.) then walk back to safa: lap 2. 6 lap 7 ends at marwah. sa‘i is complete. lap tracker you are on lap 1 of 7 safa marwah alhamdulillah sa‘i complete you should be at marwah. 1 s→m 2 m→s 3 s→m 4 m→s 5 s→m 6 m→s 7 s→m i reached the hill +1 undo what do i say? approaching safa, first lap only إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ مِنْ شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ ۝ أَبْدَأُ بِمَا بَدَأَ اللَّهُ بِهِ inna-ṣ-ṣafā wa-l-marwata min sha‘ā’iri-llāh. abda’u bimā bada’a-llāhu bih. meaning: indeed safa and marwah are among the signs of allah. i begin with what allah began with. qur’an 2:158 · sahih muslim 1218 on safa and on marwah, facing the ka‘bah اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ. لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ، أَنْجَزَ وَعْدَهُ، وَنَصَرَ عَبْدَهُ، وَهَزَمَ الْأَحْزَابَ وَحْدَهُ allāhu akbar (×3). lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdahū lā sharīka lah, lahu-l-mulku wa lahu-l-ḥamd, wa huwa ‘alā kulli shay’in qadīr. lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdah, anjaza wa‘dah, wa naṣara ‘abdah, wa hazama-l-aḥzāba waḥdah. meaning: allah is the greatest. none has the right to be worshipped but allah alone, without partner. his is the dominion and the praise, and he has power over all things. none has the right to be worshipped but allah alone. he fulfilled his promise, helped his servant, and alone defeated the allied forces. sahih muslim 1218 · say it 3 times, with your own dua in between while walking: your own words no fixed dua is required between the hills. make dua, dhikr or recite qur’an. ideas for dhikr remember you may rest and drink sit down between laps if you need to. wudu is recommended for sa‘i, but most scholars say it is not required. wheelchair? sa‘i in a wheelchair is valid. there are wheelchair lanes and upper floors. care guidance avoid these mistakes starting at marwah. that first lap doesn’t count. counting there-and-back as one lap. safa → marwah is one; marwah → safa is the next. running the whole way. the light jog is only for men, only between the green lights. back next · step 8 shave or cut hair

title: Step 8 · Halq or Taqsir
text: step 8 of 8 halq / taqsir 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 08 · essential · last step shave or shorten your hair this is the last act of umrah. it ends your ihram. halq = shave. taqsir = shorten. where am i? after sa‘i: barbers near the marwah exits, or your hotel what do i do now? men must a shave the whole head. this is better: the prophet ﷺ made dua three times for those who shave. best b or shorten hair from all over the head. not just a few strands from one side. scholars differ on the minimum women must 1 gather your hair together. in private: at your hotel, by yourself, a mahram, or another woman. 2 cut about a fingertip’s length from the ends. roughly 2 cm. women do not shave. what do i say? nothing specific is required. thank allah in your own words. a simple word of thanks الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ al-ḥamdu lillāh meaning: all praise is for allah. remember use a new, clean blade ask the barber to open a fresh blade in front of you. avoid changing out of ihram clothes, or using perfume, before your hair is cut. dua for those who shave: sahih al-bukhari 1727, sahih muslim 1301 · women shorten, not shave: sunan abi dawud 1984 back finish umrah complete

title: Umrah complete
text: all 8 steps done umrah complete الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ your umrah is complete. may allah accept it from you. what changes now? all ihram restrictions are lifted. you may wear normal clothes and use perfume. keep praying in the masjid and doing extra (voluntary) tawaf, which needs no ihram. a greeting pilgrims share تَقَبَّلَ اللَّهُ مِنَّا وَمِنْكُمْ taqabbala-llāhu minnā wa minkum meaning: may allah accept from us and from you. farewell tawaf when leaving makkah? required after hajj. for umrah, scholars differ. many recommend it. ask your scholar. what comes next? visiting madinah (optional, not part of umrah) going to madinah? book a free rawdah (riyad al-jannah) permit in the nusuk app before you go; you can only enter in your time slot. the haramain train takes about 2 hours from makkah to madinah. duas to keep making share this free guide with family back to home

title: Duas and Dhikr by moment
text: guidance duas & dhikr ihram masjid tawaf after tawaf safa & marwah any time d · organised by moment what to say, and when you may always use your own words dua can be made in any language. only a few moments have a wording from the sunnah, shown below. 1 entering ihram intention, at the meeqat لَبَّيْكَ عُمْرَةً labbayka ‘umratan meaning: here i am, o allah, for umrah. based on the prophet’s ﷺ wording “labbayka ‘umratan wa ḥajjan” for umrah with hajj · sahih muslim 1251 talbiyah, until tawaf begins لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ labbayka-llāhumma labbayk. labbayka lā sharīka laka labbayk. inna-l-ḥamda wa-n-ni‘mata laka wa-l-mulk. lā sharīka lak. meaning: here i am, o allah, here i am. here i am, you have no partner, here i am. all praise and blessings are yours, and all dominion. you have no partner. sahih al-bukhari 1549 · sahih muslim 1184 optional condition, if you fear you can’t finish اللَّهُمَّ مَحِلِّي حَيْثُ حَبَسْتَنِي allāhumma maḥillī ḥaythu ḥabastanī meaning: o allah, i will leave ihram wherever you stop me. sahih al-bukhari 5089 · sahih muslim 1207 2 entering & leaving the masjid entering, right foot first بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ، اللَّهُمَّ افْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ bismillāh, wa-ṣ-ṣalātu wa-s-salāmu ‘alā rasūlillāh. allāhumma-ftaḥ lī abwāba raḥmatik. meaning: in the name of allah, and peace and blessings on the messenger of allah. o allah, open for me the doors of your mercy. sahih muslim 713 · sunan abi dawud 465 leaving, left foot first اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ allāhumma innī as’aluka min faḍlik. meaning: o allah, i ask you from your bounty. sahih muslim 713 3 during tawaf at the black stone, each round اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ allāhu akbar meaning: allah is the greatest. sahih al-bukhari 1613 yemeni corner → black stone رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ rabbanā ātinā fi-d-dunyā ḥasanah, wa fi-l-ākhirati ḥasanah, wa qinā ‘adhāba-n-nār. meaning: our lord, give us good in this world and good in the hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the fire. qur’an 2:201 · sunan abi dawud 1892 for the rest of each round there is no fixed dua. use the dhikr at the bottom of this page or your own words. 4 after tawaf going to maqam ibrahim وَاتَّخِذُوا مِنْ مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ مُصَلًّى wattakhidhū min maqāmi ibrāhīma muṣallā. meaning: and take the standing place of ibrahim as a place of prayer. qur’an 2:125 · sahih muslim 1218 zamzam any dua, in your own words. “zamzam water is for whatever it is drunk for.” sunan ibn majah 3062 5 safa & marwah approaching safa, first time only إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ مِنْ شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ ۝ أَبْدَأُ بِمَا بَدَأَ اللَّهُ بِهِ inna-ṣ-ṣafā wa-l-marwata min sha‘ā’iri-llāh. abda’u bimā bada’a-llāhu bih. meaning: indeed safa and marwah are among the signs of allah. i begin with what allah began with. qur’an 2:158 · sahih muslim 1218 on each hill, facing the ka‘bah (×3) لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ، أَنْجَزَ وَعْدَهُ، وَنَصَرَ عَبْدَهُ، وَهَزَمَ الْأَحْزَابَ وَحْدَهُ lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdahū lā sharīka lah, lahu-l-mulku wa lahu-l-ḥamd, wa huwa ‘alā kulli shay’in qadīr. lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdah, anjaza wa‘dah, wa naṣara ‘abdah, wa hazama-l-aḥzāba waḥdah. meaning: none has the right to be worshipped but allah alone, without partner. his is the dominion and the praise, and he has power over all things. none has the right to be worshipped but allah alone. he fulfilled his promise, helped his servant, and alone defeated the allied forces. sahih muslim 1218 · begin with “allāhu akbar” ×3 between the hills (from the companions) رَبِّ اغْفِرْ وَارْحَمْ، إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْأَعَزُّ الْأَكْرَمُ rabbi-ghfir warḥam, innaka anta-l-a‘azzu-l-akram. meaning: my lord, forgive and have mercy. you are the most mighty, the most generous. reported from companions, not from the prophet ﷺ · musannaf ibn abi shaybah (book of hajj); al-bayhaqi, al-sunan al-kubra 5/95 6 any time سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ subḥāna-llāh glory be to allah الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ al-ḥamdu lillāh all praise is for allah لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ lā ilāha illa-llāh none is worthy of worship but allah اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ allāhu akbar allah is the greatest أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ astaghfiru-llāh i ask allah’s forgiveness اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَىٰ مُحَمَّدٍ allāhumma ṣalli ‘alā muḥammad o allah, send blessings on muhammad

title: Women’s guidance
text: special guidance women e · women’s guidance umrah for women the steps are the same as for men, with a few differences. here they are, step by step. 2 ihram wear your normal loose, modest clothes, in any colour. there is no special ihram garment for women. do not wear a niqab (face veil) or gloves while in ihram. say the talbiyah quietly. covering the face near men many scholars allow lowering a cloth from the head over the face when non-mahram men are near. follow your scholar. no niqab or gloves: sahih al-bukhari 1838. the report of women lowering a cloth (sunan abi dawud 1833) is graded weak by al-albani; scholars rely on other reports. 5 tawaf & 7 sa‘i keep both shoulders covered. the right-shoulder uncovering is for men only. walk at a normal pace. no brisk walking in tawaf, no jogging between the green lights. you don’t need to reach the black stone. pointing is enough. in crowds, the outer edges and upper floors are calmer. 8 cutting hair gather your hair and cut about a fingertip’s length (≈2 cm) from the ends, in private. women do not shave. sunan abi dawud 1984 if your period starts don’t worry. your umrah is not lost. here is what to do. a before ihram? you can still enter ihram at the meeqat. take a bath for cleanliness, make the intention and say the talbiyah. b before tawaf? stay in ihram. do everything except tawaf. when your period ends, take a full bath (ghusl), then do tawaf, sa‘i and cut your hair. c after tawaf, before sa‘i? continue. you can do sa‘i and cut your hair. d your flight leaves before it ends? scholars give different answers. speak to a scholar before you travel if you can. “do everything a pilgrim does, except tawaf of the house, until you are clean.” sahih al-bukhari 305. ihram after childbirth bleeding: sahih muslim 1209. staying inside the masjid during a period most scholars say don’t stay in the masjid; some allow it. follow your scholar. medicine to delay a period many scholars permit it if it is safe for you. ask your doctor first. travelling travelling without a mahram saudi rules: since october 2022 the ministry of hajj and umrah no longer requires women to have a mahram for umrah. religious ruling: scholars differ. ask your scholar. back to step 5 · tawaf

title: Elderly, disabled and special circumstances
text: special guidance care & access e · special circumstances umrah is for everyone islam makes things easy. if walking, standing or crowds are hard for you, there is a way. elderly disabilities families first-timers good to know: these are all valid tawaf and sa‘i in a wheelchair or electric cart. the prophet ﷺ did tawaf riding, and told umm salamah, who was ill, to do tawaf riding. tawaf on the upper floors or roof. resting between tawaf and sa‘i, and sitting between laps of sa‘i. skipping sunnah acts you can’t do: brisk walking, jogging, touching the black stone. sahih al-bukhari 1607, 1619 elderly pilgrims 1 add the condition when entering ihram. “allāhumma maḥillī ḥaythu ḥabastanī.” if illness stops you, you can leave ihram without penalty. see step 2 2 rest first. go at quieter, cooler times. late night and early morning are usually calmer. 3 ask for a wheelchair or cart at the masjid. ask staff at the gates where to find them today; locations and options change. 4 carry water, medicines and a small snack. people with disabilities can’t walk? you may be pushed or carried for tawaf and sa‘i. low vision or blind? go with a companion. this guide works with screen readers, large text and audio. deaf or hard of hearing? every dua has written transliteration and meaning; agree hand signals with your group. can’t cut your own hair? anyone may cut it for you. continuous bleeding or incontinence many scholars say make wudu after the time for prayer begins and do tawaf with it. ask a scholar about your case. families & children a child’s umrah is valid , and the parent is rewarded. for a young child, the parent makes the intention and carries them. sahih muslim 1336 1 put an id band on every child. your phone number, hotel name and the child’s name. 2 photo each child every morning. so you can show what they are wearing today. 3 agree a meeting gate and teach it. “if you are lost, stay still and tell a guard: gate [number].” 4 take turns. one adult does tawaf while another rests with small children. check current rules for prams in the mataf. first-time pilgrims it is normal to feel overwhelmed. stop, breathe, open this guide. only 4 things are essential. everything else is a bonus. walk on the outer edge of the crowd. it is longer but calmer. use the round and lap counters so you don’t worry about counting. when unsure, ask your group leader or a scholar at the masjid. back to umrah steps

title: Common mistakes and questions
text: help mistakes & questions f · common mistakes easy to avoid, once you know ! can affect validity etiquette / sunnah ! can affect validity · step 2 passing the meeqat without entering ihram. enter ihram before. if it already happened, ask a scholar straight away (going back, or a compensation). ! can affect validity · step 5 walking through hijr isma‘il (the curved wall). walk outside it. a round through it doesn’t count; repeat that round. ! can affect validity · step 7 starting sa‘i at marwah, or counting there-and-back as one lap. start at safa. each one-way walk is one lap. finish at marwah. ! can affect validity · step 8 men cutting only a few hairs; leaving ihram before cutting. shave, or shorten from all over the head. cut first, then change clothes. sunnah · step 5 keeping the right shoulder bare all through ihram, even in prayer. bare it only during this tawaf. cover it for prayer. etiquette · step 5 pushing and hurting people to kiss the black stone. point with your right hand. kissing it is sunnah; harming others is not allowed. etiquette thinking a special dua must be read for each round, or reading loudly from a book in a group. speak to allah softly, in your own words. quick questions i lost count of my rounds. go with the lower number you are sure of, and continue. can i rest between tawaf and sa‘i? yes. do i need wudu for sa‘i? it is recommended. most scholars say it is not required. the prayer started during tawaf or sa‘i. join the prayer. then continue from where you stopped. i used scented soap by mistake. wash it off. if you forgot or didn’t know, most scholars say there is no penalty. can i shower in ihram? yes, with unscented soap. a few hairs falling out by accident is not a problem. must i touch or kiss the black stone? no. pointing toward it is enough. is tawaf on the upper floors valid? yes. still unsure? ask your group leader or a scholar at the masjid. scholarly notes

title: Quick reference · Pocket mode
text: g · pocket mode quick reference umrah on one screen large text. works offline. tap a step for full detail. 1 ihram at the meeqat: intend umrah. men in 2 white sheets. “labbayka ‘umratan” · then the talbiyah 2 tawaf · 7 rounds start and end at the black stone. ka‘bah on your left . outside hijr isma‘il. need wudu. “allāhu akbar” at the black stone · “rabbanā ātinā…” before it 3 pray 2 · zamzam 2 rak‘ahs behind maqam ibrahim or anywhere. drink zamzam, make dua. 4 sa‘i · 7 laps start safa , end marwah. safa → marwah = 1 lap. men jog between green lights. on each hill: face the ka‘bah, “allāhu akbar” ×3, dhikr, dua 5 hair men: shave, or shorten all over. women: fingertip length. done ihram is over. alhamdulillah. counters tawaf not started sa‘i not started my info · show to a helper saved only on this phone. nothing is sent anywhere. my name hotel name & area group leader’s phone our meeting gate emergency in makkah: call 911 saudi arabia’s unified emergency number (police, ambulance, fire) for the makkah region. source: saudi press agency, june 2026 show my info full-screen printable a4 quick card

title: Sources and scholarly notes
text: reference sources & notes for those who want more how this guide handles differences the main steps follow widely held positions. where recognised schools of fiqh differ, we say so with a scholars differ label and explain here. if you follow a particular school or scholar, follow them. review status content to be reviewed and signed off by [reviewing scholar / institution] before publication. version [x.x], [date]. scholarly notes is umrah obligatory? shafi‘i and hanbali scholars: obligatory once in a lifetime for those able. hanafi and maliki scholars: a strongly emphasised sunnah. “essential” acts schools differ on which acts are pillars (rukn) and which are obligations (wajib). the guide calls all four “essential” because every pilgrim performs them. wudu for tawaf the majority hold it is a condition. hanafi scholars hold it is obligatory but not a condition. if wudu breaks mid-tawaf, views differ on continuing or restarting. ihram prayer many scholars recommend 2 rak‘ahs before ihram. others hold there is no prayer specific to ihram, and one enters ihram after an obligatory prayer if it is time. two rak‘ahs after tawaf the majority: sunnah. hanafi scholars: wajib. views also differ on praying them at disliked times. minimum hair to cut (men) views include: the whole head, most of the head, a quarter of the head, or three hairs. shaving, or shortening from the whole head, satisfies all views. meeqat for air travellers most scholars: enter ihram before the aircraft crosses the meeqat. some consider jeddah a valid place for certain arrivals. farewell tawaf after umrah obligatory after hajj. for umrah, some scholars say obligatory, others recommended. women’s face covering in ihram niqab is not worn. many allow lowering a cloth near non-mahram men; views differ on whether it may touch the face. (the report in abu dawud 1833 is graded weak by al-albani.) menstruation and the masjid most scholars: a menstruating woman does not stay in the masjid. some permit it. what we removed, and why claims found in common booklets that we could not trace to an authentic report are left out: e.g. guaranteed acceptance of every dua at the first sight of the ka‘bah, and set duas for each round of tawaf. official rules, checked sept 2026 health (saudi ministry of health, umrah 1447h/2026) meningitis vaccine required for all umrah pilgrims: acyw/acywx conjugate within 5 years, or polysaccharide within 3 years, at least 10 days before arrival. polio and yellow fever only for listed countries. covid-19 only for 65+, pregnant women and chronic illness. permits (ministry of hajj and umrah) umrah permits are booked in the nusuk app. umrah is possible on an umrah visa or a visit/tourist visa. bookings (ministry of hajj and umrah / nusuk) umrah visas require a confirmed licensed-hotel booking recorded in nusuk masar (announced june 2025, for 1447h onward). travel sources report that ground transport must also be pre-booked for 1448h; confirm with your agent. rawdah visits need a free nusuk permit with a fixed time slot. haramain train operated by saudi arabia railways. stations: makkah, jeddah (al-sulimaniyah), king abdulaziz international airport, king abdullah economic city and madinah. makkah to madinah about 2 hours. women since october 2022 saudi rules no longer require a mahram for women performing umrah. emergency 911 is the unified emergency number in the makkah region (saudi press agency, june 2026). not officially confirmed passport validity of 6 months is widely stated by airlines and agents; we could not find it on an official saudi page. references intention wording “labbayka ‘umratan…” muslim 1251 talbiyah bukhari 1549 · muslim 1184 the meeqat bukhari 1524, 1531 · muslim 1181 clothing forbidden in ihram bukhari 1542 · muslim 1177 women: no niqab or gloves bukhari 1838 perfume before ihram bukhari 1539 · muslim 1189 condition (ishtirat) bukhari 5089 · muslim 1207 no arguing in pilgrimage qur’an 2:197 bath before entering makkah bukhari 1573 masjid entry and exit duas muslim 713 · abu dawud 465 (sahih) takbir at the black stone bukhari 1613 rabbana atina qur’an 2:201 · abu dawud 1892 (hasan) the prophet’s ﷺ pilgrimage (ramal, maqam, safa) muslim 1218 tawaf while riding bukhari 1607, 1619 zamzam ibn majah 3062 (hasan) safa and marwah qur’an 2:158 dua for those who shave bukhari 1727 · muslim 1301 women shorten, not shave abu dawud 1984 (sahih li ghayrihi) menstruation: all but tawaf bukhari 305 ihram while bleeding muslim 1209 a child’s pilgrimage muslim 1336 “rabbi-ghfir warḥam…” (companions) ibn abi shaybah · al-bayhaqi 5/95 travel dua qur’an 43:13–14 · muslim 1342 all hadith numbers and gradings checked against sunnah.com in september 2026 (gradings for the sunan collections as shown there, mostly al-albani). final sign-off still rests with the reviewing scholar.
